findings.title: Deposit is within the amount cap
findings.detail: This amount check does not verify deposit protection or authenticity. Annual rent GBP 15600; cap = 15600 / 52 * 5 (GBP 1500.00 rounded down to pennies); requested GBP 1500. Importance: 85/100. Conditional: Confirm that the rented property is in England. Confirm this is an ordinary private tenancy, not an excluded arrangement. Confirm that rent and deposit cover the same whole tenancy. The amount-cap pass holds on the quoted figures. Rent is GBP 1300 per calendar month, so annual rent is GBP 15,600 and five weeks is GBP 1,500.00. The stated deposit of GBP 1,500 is at the cap, not above it. The cap calculation is not overturned. Nothing in the contract contradicts these figures, and no holding deposit or other payment is quoted that would change the scope. The pass depends on facts the context leaves unknown: the jurisdiction (England), the tenancy type (ordinary private tenancy rather than an excluded arrangement), and whether the rent and deposit cover the same whole tenancy. The check is also limited to the amount. It says nothing about whether the deposit is protected or the arrangement is authentic. No substantive counter-evidence exists to dismiss it, so it stays conditional on those facts. Sources: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/tenant-fees-act-2019-guidance-for-tenants
